items.title: Sergey Chekashkin, Kitchener
notes: S. Chekashkin spoke to Council and recommended the use of glass beads, Johnson screens, and full cementation to increase water production in wells in the Region of Waterloo.

items.title: Mark Reusser, Vice President, The Waterloo Federation of Agriculture
notes: M. Reusser spoke to Council regarding the high costs of well interference on residents, and spoke against the Region taking water from the Wilmot aquifer.

items.title: Samantha Lernout, President. Citizens for Safe Groundwater Inc.
notes:
S. Lernout discussed concerns related to drawdown in the Wilmot Centre Aquafer and asked Council to take a proactive approach to well interferences.

S. Lernout asked Council to incorporate a ten (10) day guaranteed advance review, an independent, third-party technical expert, and mandatory baseline data sharing to the well interference policy. S. Lernout also asked Council to implement hard stop pumping levels.

Responding to a question from Council, S. Lernout confirmed that the reported well issues are primarily clustered surrounding the Wilmot well field.

Further materials from this delegation were received that are attached to the minutes.

items.title: EES-WIM-26-017, Mannheim Service Area Water Capacity Constraint - Update on Work Underway - September 2026
notes:
Ken Brothers, Commissioner of Water and Wastewater, introduced the report and provided an overview of the work underway in the Mannheim Service Area. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda.

K. Brothers summarized the projects ongoing at the Mannheim Side Stream Project, Greenbrook, the Grand River Water System, and the Maple Grove Water System.

K. Brothers stated that staff have found ways to bring more water online faster than anticipated, and that the 15 L/s being used from the Wilmot Centre Wellfield will no longer be needed after January 2027.

K. Brothers provided an update on the Interim Risk Management Framework and stated that the revised approach will reconfigure one of the pressure zones to move some demand from the Mannheim Service Area to the Middleton Service Area. K. Brothers stated that this would save the Region $8.1 million and be done three (3) years faster. K. Brothers also noted that a revised approach to the Parkway Wells could bring an additional 10L/s online two (2) years earlier than planned and would save $2.9 million.

Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services provided a growth and development update. R. Reiger confirmed that the Region has received two (2) requests for Transfers of Servicing Commitment, both of which have been fully executed, and one (1) Regional Forward Looking Servicing Agreement, which is being reviewed.

R. Regier provided a communications update, which includes a progress update scheduled for September 10, 2026, and continued website and social updates. R. Regier also stated a new landing page will be launched to support communications.

K. Brothers explained next steps, which include finalized site connection for the Mannheim side stream project, reports on infrastructure updates, and the OCWA report coming in October 2026.

Responding to a question from Council, Pam Law, Director of Water Capacity Projects, explained that instead of transferring surplus water supply from the Middleton Service Area to the whole CAM2 West via pumping, staff are able to put a portion of the demand directly into the Middle Service Area to directly and permanently utilize the water supply.

Responding to a question from Council, P. Law explained that staff will bring back a strategy update that will assess the sustainable supply and operational resilience in the Middleton Service Area. P. Law further explained that staff are committed to continue looking for opportunities to expedite or develop solutions to identify efficiencies.

In response to Council, A. Shaw confirmed that biennial reports are available to the public on the Region's website, and staff are willing to share data with residents upon request. A. Shaw stated that there is no mechanism online to provide real-time data to residents.

Responding to Council, P. Law explained that the Mannheim side stream project is expected to be running by the end of the second quarter of 2027, and that the Interim Risk Management Framework will be updated to reflect the changes in timing.

In response to Council, A. Shaw stated that a short list of options for the Water Supply Strategy will be brought back by the end of 2026, and will provide long-term options, including surface water options such as a pipeline.

Received for information.

items.title: EES-WIM-26-018, Water Capacity Constraint 2027 Resourcing Needs
notes:
K. Brothers provided an overview of the report and an explanation of the resourcing needs in the Water and Wastewater department for 2027.

Council provided direction that staff look at offsetting Full-Time Employee asks with attrition in the organization and review of temporary positions that began during the COVID-19 pandemic and became permanent.

Council provided further direction that staff also include a breakdown of staffing levels by department and division in the regional budget documents for the 2027 budget cycle.

Kate Konopka, Commissioner of Human Resources, explained that temporary position can only go up to 15 months, and once this point is reached the position would be terminated unless the union agrees to extend. K. Konopka reiterated that all permanent positions are approved by Council.

Responding to Council, A. Shaw explained that there is a shortage of operators with class one (1) licenses in the Province, and the recommendation is to recruit more junior level staff, who will then be trained and licensed within the timeframe the Region would need. A. Shaw emphasized that more staff are needed to be able to maintain and operate new infrastructure.

Received for information.

items.title: EES-WIM-26-019, Policy and Procedures for Responding to Groundwater Interference Claims in the Region of Waterloo (Well Interference Policy)
notes:
K. Brothers introduced the report and provided an overview of the draft Well Interference Policy. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda.

K. Brothers explained that the final draft policy incorporates a background review of the Region's current and past Well Interference Policies, a jurisdictional scan of other policies, and feedback from two (2) public engagement sessions and Council.

K. Brothers highlighted key updates to the policy, including the change of the term 'resident' to remove any perception that the policy only applies to private homes, the addition of one (1) non-voting member of the public added to the Appeal Committee, and details added to outline what the Consultant will be asked to provide to the appellant prior to the site visit. Other updates include changing the name of the policy to the Well Interference Claim Policy and providing clarity surrounding data sharing and emergency water supply assistance.

Council discussed amendments to the policy to enhance the data sharing requirements in the Policy,

In response to Council, A. Shaw confirmed that appellants will not need to prove that they are unable to pay in order to have their invoices directly paid by the Region

items.title: COR-TRY-26-034, Increase to C2022-14 Water Supply Strategy Update
notes:
Kedar Tupil, Commissioner of Corporate Services, introduced the report and provided an overview of the need to increase the contract with CIMA Canada for the C2022-14 Water Supply Strategy. K. Tupil explained that this is due to the additional work needed due to the water capacity constraint in the Mannheim Service Area. 

P. Law confirmed that the contract includes additional resources that will support the project team to catch up on the delays incurred through the water capacity constraint. P. Law stated that a final recommended strategy will be presented to Council by the end of 2027. 

Council gave direction to staff to provide a summary of the total costs related to the water capacity constraint. 

Responding to Council, P. Law explained that the scope of the project increased as there was a substantial amount of work that needed to be reviewed and updated following the water constraint investigation.

Responding to a question from Council, P. Law stated the consultants were asked to go through the remaining scope of work and ensure that the increase put forward would address the ability to complete the project. 

In response to Council, P. Law acknowledged the need to align growth forecast methodologies between the Region of Waterloo and it's lower-tier municipalities, and stated planning is moving forward in a way that aligns with Area Municipalities.  

Responding to Council, P. Law stated the contingency fund for this project is approximately $38,000. Council provided direction to staff to bring back information regarding the total cost for this project, including contingencies.

motions.item_title: EES-WIM-26-019, Policy and Procedures for Responding to Groundwater Interference Claims in the Region of Waterloo (Well Interference Policy)
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo endorse the revised Well Interference Policy, as amended below , attached in Appendix A and the Terms of Reference, attached in Appendix B, as outlined in EES-WIM-26-019 dated September 9, 2026: Section 4.5 Strike current language: Investigation records and data utilized to support decision making may be shared with the Appellant, upon request. Replace with: The Appellant will automatically be provided, concurrently with the Technical Evaluation, complete copies of all investigation records and data collected, obtained, reviewed, considered, relied upon or generated in connection with the investigation and Technical Evaluation for the relevant time range and with further data available upon request. Where groundwater monitoring wells are located in the vicinity of the Appellant’s Private Well, all available monitoring data from those wells will also be provided to the Appellant for information, regardless of whether that data was reviewed, considered or relied upon in completing the investigation or Technical Evaluation. Section 8 Add onto the current section: The Clerk of the Region will provide the Appeal Committee, in advance of the hearing date, all relevant information including the Consultant's Technical Assessment report and all information provided by the Appellant. Replace to read with the addition: The Clerk of the Region will provide the Appeal Committee, in advance of the hearing date, all relevant information, including the Consultant’s Technical Assessment report and all information provided by the Appellant. All information provided to the Appeal Committee will be provided concurrently and in its entirety to the Appellant, so that the Appellant and the Appeal Committee have access to the same information in advance of the hearing. Any additional information subsequently provided to the Appeal Committee prior to the hearing will also be provided to the Appellant at the same time.

Where groundwater monitoring wells are located in the vicinity of the Appellant’s Private Well, all available monitoring data from those wells will also be provided to the Appellant for information, regardless of whether that data was reviewed, considered or relied upon in completing the investigation or Technical Evaluation.

Section 8

Add onto the current section: The Clerk of the Region will provide the Appeal Committee, in advance of the hearing date, all relevant information including the Consultant's Technical Assessment report and all information provided by the Appellant.

Replace to read with the addition: The Clerk of the Region will provide the Appeal Committee, in advance of the hearing date, all relevant information, including the Consultant’s Technical Assessment report and all information provided by the Appellant. All information provided to the Appeal Committee will be provided concurrently and in its entirety to the Appellant, so that the Appellant and the Appeal Committee have access to the same information in advance of the hearing. Any additional information subsequently provided to the Appeal Committee prior to the hearing will also be provided to the Appellant at the same time.
